name: ProtGPT3
reason: Primary preprint verified via bioRxiv API: DOI 10.64898/2026.06.04.730041, 'ProtGPT3: an Open-source family of Promptable and Aligned Protein Language Models', Garibbo/Boxo Corominas/Stocco/Illanes Vicioso/Middendorf/Ferruz, corresponding Michele Garibbo (Centre for Genomic Regulation), posted 2026-06-08, v1, cc_by, not withdrawn, published_doi NA. Artifacts verified officially owned: HF org AI4PD ('AI for protein design', the Ferruz-lab org that also hosts ProtGPT2 and ZymCTRL) carries exactly 7 ProtGPT3 checkpoints (112M, 1.3B, 10B, MSA, and 112M/1.3B/10B-dpo), all gated:false, all with safetensors weights; collection slug AI4PD/protgpt3-family-694961c1c66f557bc5a62e00 confirmed via HF collections API (gating:false). Code repo github.com/michele1993/protGPT3 (first/corresponding author's account, created 2026-05-07) contains the pretraining, DPO-alignment, SFT-vs-prompting and MSA test-time-compute code. Scope is unambiguous: pretrained autoregressive pLM family, reusable for unconditional generation, prefix/family-conditioned generation, few-shot MSA prompting, and variant-effect scoring (ProteinGym results in the appendix). LICENCE CAVEAT, load-bearing: none of the 7 model cards declares a license field (cardData has no 'license' key on any of them), no LICENSE file exists in the code repo or in any HF repo, and the only affirmative statement is the paper's Appendix A.18 wording quoted below. noncommercial is set false on the strength of the authors' explicit 'open source' release statement plus ungated public weights, but no formal grant document exists - the parent should treat the licence as UNSPECIFIED rather than as a verified permissive licence.
licence_quote: Paper Appendix A.18 (fetched PDF): 'All 7 models are publicly available open source on Hugging Face Hub at https://huggingface.co/collections/AI4PD/protgpt3-family. The entire code base for training and evaluation is available on a GitHub repository at https://github.com/michele1993/protGPT3.' No SPDX licence is declared anywhere: HF cardData for AI4PD/ProtGPT3-112M, -1.3B, -10B, -MSA, -112M-dpo has no 'license' key, no LICENSE file among the repo siblings, and github.com/michele1993/protGPT3 returns license:null from the GitHub API. Preprint text itself is CC-BY 4.0 (bioRxiv record license: cc_by).

record.name: ProtGPT3
record.description: Open-source family of autoregressive protein language models from the Ferruz lab (CRG), spanning 112M to 10B parameters in a Mixtral-style sparse mixture-of-experts architecture, with DPO-aligned variants and a 112M MSA-promptable model for homolog-conditioned few-shot generation. Seven checkpoints are released on Hugging Face together with training, alignment and inference-time-compute code.
record.io: amino-acid prefix with an N-to-C/C-to-N direction token, or a prompt of ~15 homologous sequences for the MSA model -> generated protein sequences and per-sequence likelihoods
record.status: Open weights, 7 ungated checkpoints on Hugging Face (AI4PD org); paper states an open-source release but no formal licence is declared on the model cards or code repo
record.use_cases: de novo protein sequence generation, family-conditioned and few-shot homolog-prompted design, DPO-aligned low-complexity reduction, zero-shot variant effect scoring, enzyme design (defluorinase case study)

record.name: MSA Pairformer
record.description: 111M-parameter MSA-based protein language model that adapts the AlphaFold Pairformer's bidirectional sequence<->pair representation updates into a pretrained LM of protein and protein-protein coevolution. Reported to outperform ESM2-15B on unsupervised contact prediction with two orders of magnitude fewer parameters, and to substantially improve contact prediction at protein-protein interfaces; published in Cell in 2026 after a 2025 preprint and weight release.
record.io: query sequence plus its multiple sequence alignment -> sequence and pairwise embeddings, residue-residue contact maps (monomer and interface), zero-shot variant effect scores
record.status: Open weights and code under a modified MIT licence explicitly permitting commercial use; Hugging Face repo ungated
record.use_cases: protein sequence embedding, unsupervised residue-residue contact prediction, protein-protein interface contact prediction, screening of interacting sequence pairs, zero-shot variant effect prediction

record.name: ProLLaMA
record.description: Llama-2-7B-based multitask protein large language model trained in two stages - continued pretraining on protein sequences (ProLLaMA_Stage_1) followed by instruction tuning - so that a single model handles both controllable superfamily-conditioned sequence generation and protein understanding tasks such as superfamily prediction. Accepted by IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence in 2025 per the arXiv metadata.
record.io: natural-language instruction such as '[Generate by superfamily] Superfamily=<...>' or '[Determine superfamily] Seq=<...>', optionally with an amino-acid prefix -> generated protein sequence or predicted superfamily label
record.status: Open weights on Hugging Face (ungated); code Apache-2.0, weights derived from Llama-2-7B and subject to the Llama 2 licence
record.use_cases: controllable protein sequence generation by superfamily, prefix-conditioned generation, protein superfamily prediction, mutation-effect scripting, general protein LM backbone for instruction-style tasks

record.name: UTRGen
record.description: Unified 5' UTR modelling framework built on a small GPT-2 decoder (8 layers, 16 heads, 384 hidden, 256-token context) autoregressively pretrained on multi-species 5' UTR sequence and then adapted, via lightweight prediction heads, to translation efficiency, expression level, mean ribosome load and IRES identification, plus GRPO-based function-guided sequence design. Reported state of the art across 14 benchmark datasets.
record.io: single-nucleotide prompt or 5' UTR sequence -> generated 5' UTR sequences (FASTA), or predicted translation efficiency / expression level / mean ribosome load / IRES class
record.status: MIT-licensed code on GitHub; pretrained checkpoints distributed as a publicly shared Google Drive archive
record.use_cases: de novo 5' UTR generation, translation efficiency and expression level prediction, mean ribosome load prediction, IRES identification, reinforcement-learning-guided mRNA UTR design

name: Shifu-LMR
reason: THE CORE JOB FOR THIS CANDIDATE IS DONE: the official artifact exists and I located it. A GitHub code search for 'Shifu-Corpus' surfaced github.com/Vicens-Lab/LMR - the org is the Vicens Lab, and the repo LICENSE names 'Gabriel Galvez and Quentin Vicens, Vicens Lab, Center for Nuclear Receptors and Cell Signaling, University of Houston', exactly matching the preprint's authors and corresponding institution, and its CITATION points at this preprint's DOI. The discovery lane missed it because the repo and the weight repos are named LMR, not Shifu. Repo created 2026-07-03, pushed 2026-07-17, MIT, not archived. Weights verified: four Hugging Face repos under GaboG7 (= Gabriel Cardenas Galvez, first author), all created 2026-07-03, all gated:false, private:false, each declaring license 'mit' and tagged 'shifu', each containing a real .pt checkpoint - LMR-v0 (289M, lmr_v0.pt, 3.47 GB), LMR-G (228M, lmr_g.pt, 2.74 GB), LMR-mini (65M = the paper's Shifu-LMR-Nano, lmr_mini.pt, 0.76 GB), LMR-Long (290M, 4096 context, lmr_long.pt, 3.47 GB). Preprint verified via bioRxiv API: DOI 10.64898/2026.07.15.738762, Galvez & Vicens, posted 2026-07-16, v1, cc_by_nc, not withdrawn. SCOPE, addressing the discovery lane's second caveat: these are masked-language-model-pretrained RNA backbones (HF pipeline_tag fill-mask), and the README offers them as 'a compact RNA language-model backbone to fine-tune', with configs and training code for continued pretraining and fine-tuning - that clears pretrained/reusable/broader-than-one-task, even though every evaluation in the paper is secondary structure. LANE SPLIT for the parent: Shifu-Corpus (HF dataset GaboG7/SHIFU-Corpus, 254,123 sequences, gated:false) and the Shifu Trifecta evaluation protocol are benchmark-lane items and should be filed separately, not folded into this record. Two caveats worth carrying: the 86M LMR-G variant is explicitly NOT released, and the 2D structure heads in models_2d/ are 'config only; no weights/scripts', so only the four foundational backbones are actually downloadable. Adoption is currently near zero (1 GitHub star, 0 reported HF downloads).

The preprint TEXT is cc_by_nc per the bioRxiv record - that NC term covers the manuscript only, not the code or weights.

record.name: Shifu-LMR
record.description: Family of compact masked-language-model RNA backbones released as the model component of the Shifu framework, spanning 65M to 290M parameters including a 4,096-token long-context variant. The 65M Shifu-LMR-Nano is reported to reach micro-F1 0.789 on RNA secondary structure against RiNALMo's 0.627 at 650M parameters, and the family is released as fine-tunable backbones alongside the leakage-audited Shifu-Corpus dataset and the three-axis Shifu Trifecta evaluation protocol.
record.io: RNA nucleotide sequence -> contextual residue embeddings and masked-token predictions, fine-tunable to base-pair / secondary-structure predictions
record.status: Open weights: four MIT-licensed, ungated checkpoints on Hugging Face; code MIT on GitHub
record.use_cases: RNA sequence representation learning, RNA secondary structure prediction after fine-tuning, leakage-free benchmarking baseline, laptop-scale RNA language modelling and continued pretraining
